To start, could you tell me about the movement practice or sport that has been the most central to your life so far?
Options: [Team-based field sports | Endurance training and distance running | Gymnastics or technical movement arts]

As you look toward the next chapter of your sporting journey, what aspect of the discipline drives you the most?
Options: [The competitive rush of chasing podiums and shaving seconds off a personal best. | The meditative, solitary challenge of pushing into ultra-distances and testing mental stamina. | Integrating technical strength and movement to build a more versatile, tactical approach to racing.]
The meditative, solitary challenge of pushing into ultra-distances and testing mental stamina.

To better understand how your physical chapter is currently shaped, how would you describe the nature of your training rhythm and your approach to the work?
Options: [A rigorous, structured regimen where every split and interval is monitored to maximize physiological output. | An intuitive, self-guided practice that prioritizes the 'feel' of the movement and spontaneous exploration of the terrain. | A science-led approach focused on mobility, recovery, and structural resilience to sustain heavy training loads over years.]
A rigorous, structured regimen where every split and interval is monitored to maximize physiological output.

Since you have the fundamentals of a rigorous, structured training mindset, do you prefer your athletic environment to be shaped by deep, internal focus—where the primary competitor is your own potential—or by the external pressure of a team or coach who challenges you to hit those high-stakes targets?
Options: [I prefer a solitary, self-monitored environment where I am the sole architect of my progress. | I thrive on high-pressure environments where coaches and experts push me to exceed what I thought was possible.]
I prefer a solitary, self-monitored environment where I am the sole architect of my progress.

scouting_result.scout_verdict:
At 17 years old, you possess the lean, 172cm, 62kg frame of a natural endurance athlete, but it is your discipline that truly sets you apart. In the world of high-performance cycling, you have found the perfect environment for your self-architected training—a space where you are the sole controller of every cadence and watt. As you approach The Los Angeles 2028 Games, the road stretches out as a blank canvas where your rigorous, data-driven approach transforms physical effort into a work of precise, calculated art.

Unlike those who rely on external coaching to ignite their fire, you find clarity in the solitude of the long ride. This path rewards your analytical mind, allowing you to fine-tune your performance through meticulous split-tracking and constant self-assessment. Here, the machine is not just the bicycle beneath you—it is your own body, shaped and honed by a relentless internal drive to find the limit of what is possible when you are the only one in the pilot's seat.

Your commitment to the T54 marathon discipline creates a completely different, more visceral experience of the road. The T54 classification refers to athletes with impairment in the lower limbs who compete in a seated position, necessitating a powerful, sustained integration of the core and upper body to drive the racing chair forward. This path shifts the focus away from the rhythmic mechanics of standing cycling and moves it toward the intense, kinetic dialogue between your shoulders, your core, and the tarmac beneath you.

At The Los Angeles 2028 Games, you lean into the meditative, solitary challenge that has always defined your journey. While your standing training was about precision and external data, the T54 pathway is about the profound mental stamina required to endure the grueling distance of a marathon from a seated position. It is here, in the quiet, intense rhythmic grind of the push-rim, that you discover a different side of your athleticism—one that relies on a raw, internal resilience to maintain speed and focus when the miles demand everything you have.

eval_result.summary: A strong, highly tailored scouting report that effectively translates the user's data-driven, solitary endurance mindset into two compelling pathways.

authenticity.reasoning: The 'Road Machine' and 'Long Haul' archetypes perfectly fit a 172cm, 62kg frame and naturally align with a preference for solitary, endurance-based challenges.

personalization.reasoning: The verdict masterfully weaves in specific interview choices, explicitly referencing the user's 'self-architected training' and 'rigorous, data-driven approach'.

distinctness.reasoning: The two pathways contrast well: the standing profile focuses on the calculated metrics of cycling, while the adaptive T54 profile highlights the visceral, upper-body kinetic grind of wheelchair racing.

interview_quality.reasoning: The questions logically narrow the athlete's psychological profile, moving from general sport interest to specific motivations and environmental preferences with meaningful distinct options.
